summary: A draft list of ARPANET host names from Richard Watson at the Network Information Center. Starred entries are the names hosts asked for, others are assigned, and the author asks for corrections before a deadline in order to publish an official list.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC circulates a draft list of ARPANET host names, nicknames and addresses. It asks host representatives to send corrections before the author publishes a list considered official.

questions: what host names were proposed in rfc 280
subtitle: A draft list of formal host names, nicknames and ARPANET addresses.

tldr.problem: The RFC presents a draft set of host names and invites representatives to correct or change entries.
tldr.mechanism: The table lists formal names, optional nicknames and network addresses; an asterisk marks names desired by the host.

sections.title: A Draft Host List
sections.content:
Richard W. Watson says the enclosed list of host names is a draft. Names marked with an asterisk are the names desired by those hosts; the others are assigned names.

If host representatives do not send changes or corrections by December 3, the author will publish a list that everyone can consider official.
sections.plainLanguage: The names in this list are still open to correction. Hosts can request changes before the stated deadline.

sections.title: Names, Nicknames and Addresses
sections.content:
The table has columns for formal name, nickname and network address. Examples include SRI-ARC with the nickname NIC and address 2, UCLA-CCN with the nickname CCN and address 65, and BBN-NCC with the nickname NCC and address 5.

Some entries do not show a nickname or address. The RFC presents the data as a draft, so it does not establish that every value is final.
sections.plainLanguage: Each row can identify a host by its full name, a shorter nickname and a network number. An asterisk shows the name the host requested.

sections.title: The List's Status
sections.content:
This is a draft set of names, not a final directory. The author plans to publish an official list after the requested correction period if representatives do not submit changes.

The unit metadata lists RFC 280 as Unknown and records no updates or replacements.
sections.plainLanguage: The list is provisional, and the RFC describes a plan to finalize it after review. Its metadata lists status as Unknown.
